exposure: Severity of proteinuria during pregnancy (mild: 300-1000 mg/day, moderate: 1000-3500 mg/day, severe: >3500 mg/day)
cohort: The study included 142 women diagnosed with proteinuria during pregnancy.
finding: Moderate and severe proteinuria during pregnancy are significantly associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, including higher rates of prematurity, low birth weight, neonatal asphyxia, foetal growth restriction, and neonatal intensive care unit admission, compared to mild proteinuria.
